business_problem: Palmerston North City Council needed to break data out of spreadsheets and siloed on-premises systems so citizen services, regulatory workflows, and AI initiatives could run on trusted real-time information instead of slow manual handoffs.
solution_summary: Palmerston North City Council deployed Confluent Cloud as the backbone of a shift-left, event-sourced data architecture for civic operations. Every piece of data - whether it arrives from IoT devices, APIs, supplier files, finance systems, or regulatory applications - now flows through the managed streaming platform first, where governance and reuse are applied at the source. Kafka topics hold the history of data products, which the council then syncs into relational, NoSQL, time-series, and lake environments as needed. On top of that base, PNCC created reusable Property 360 datasets, real-time AI-assisted invoice processing, human-in-the-loop AI agents for resource-consent workflows, and smart-city monitoring that streams insights from hundreds of cameras and sensors. The architecture lets departments share one governed source of truth, shortens response times for citizen issues, and provides auditable orchestration for automation without handing final decisions to AI.
